key_insight: A mediation layer on top of free communication is the most effective mechanism for keeping self-interested agents cooperative and maintaining market stability, even under adversarial trolling.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests that formal governance mechanisms can materially improve resilience in multi-agent economic or workflow systems where agents optimize self-interest rather than global utility.
method: Simulated a marketplace with 18 DeepSeek-V3 agents assigned complementary production roles and constrained by a social network.
Compared 8 market mechanisms across 200 rounds with progressive troll injection.
Red-teamed the best mechanism, Mediation, using iteratively prompt-optimized LLM trolls.
evidence_signal: Across the mechanism comparison, Mediation ranked best; in adversarial testing, the strongest attack (v6) reduced honest-agent utility by 13.3% but did not collapse the market.
watch_item: Results come from a specific LLM-agent simulation setup, so performance may not directly transfer to different models, networks, or real-world economic settings.
paper_title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
